reason: The text presupposes and reinforces that the Hebrews' (Israel's) primary identity and foundational relationship is with Yahweh. They are consistently identified as 'benei Yisrael' (children of Israel/God's people), and the entire narrative structure—from their movement under Yahweh's direction ('al-pi YHWH'), through their crisis, to Yahweh's direct intervention and the commemorative naming of the place—demonstrates that their existence and survival are fundamentally bound to their relationship with Yahweh. The text shows this as a defining reality that persists even when their faith wavers. The critique of their complaining and testing of Yahweh actually presupposes this primary relationship; they are tested precisely because they belong to Yahweh and are expected to trust Him.
